sources.title: Avishai Ben-Dror: Cartographic knowledge, colonialized-colonizer spaces: Egyptian maps of Harar, 1875 to 1885 (2022)
sources.note: Indexed original article introduction read; direct fetch returned 403. Occupation late 1875 to mid-1885; mapping, administration, economic and coercive changes. Imported polygon independently decoded in identities.json.

sources.title: Avishai Ben-Dror: The Egyptian Hikimdāriya of Harar and its Hinterland, dissertation abstract (2008)
sources.note: Direct eight-page English dissertation abstract read. Printed Roman-numbered pages I to V cover occupation, Ra’uf, Gordon, contested hinterland and restoration of Emir Abdallahi. This is the author’s abstract, not the full dissertation.

sources.title: Ethiopian authorities: Harar Jugol World Heritage nomination (2004)
sources.note: Official UNESCO-hosted nomination downloaded and extracted locally as harar-nomination.pdf/txt. Contemporary buildings and craft observations dated to the nomination, not automatically projected into the 1870s. Aw Ansar historical attribution is explicit. Hospital primacy conflicts across sources, so no first-hospital claim is made.

sources.title: Bernhard Lindahl, Nordic Africa Institute: Local History of Ethiopia, Harar to Hardin (2005)
sources.note: Direct PDF read, page 6: Egyptian building programme, hospital and Muhammad Mukhtar’s account of women’s work, with references to Gill 1991 and Trimingham 1952. Used as a clearly attributed institutional historical compilation. Erroneous 1978 date and 1884 collapse date in adjacent text are not adopted; Ben-Dror supplies chronology.

sources.title: Adam Nieuważny: Civil status documents from Harar under Egyptian Administration 1875 to 1885 (2021)
sources.note: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record directly read: University of Warsaw Department of Arabic and Islamic Studies; marriage contracts, divorces and manumissions. Full text at Warsaw was inaccessible; no individual case, translated document or Arabic sample is inferred from the abstract.

sources.title: Sana Mirza: From Harar to Diu: Circulation and Reception of a Qur’anic Manuscript across the Indian Ocean (2025)
sources.note: Full original article read. Princeton Islamic Manuscripts Third Series 900q is dated stylistically to the late eighteenth century; its earlier colophon is questioned. The sample follows the author’s exact scholarly transliteration and English gloss in Developed for a Harari Market, not a reconstruction of Arabic glyphs. Contemporary 1875 bookbinder witness is distinguished from the earlier manuscript.

sources.title: Spanish state archives PARES: Protectorado español de Marruecos
sources.note: Indexed official authority entry read; direct fetch returned 429. Treaty 27 November 1912, northern protectorate ending 7 April 1956, separate southern-zone exception. Geometry independently decoded in identities.json.

sources.title: Gaceta de Madrid, 27 January 1916: organization of the protectorate
sources.note: Direct full official PDF text read. Printed pp. 209 to 211, especially article 5 on control of khalifal decrees and articles 7, 9 and 11 on schools, health and public works. Law records formal powers, not proof of uniform implementation.

sources.title: Gaceta de Madrid, 6 December 1912: proposed ratification of the Franco-Spanish convention
sources.note: Direct official PDF text read, printed p. 640, human PDF p. 2, royal decree of 5 December. Exact phrase Convenio entre España y Francia appears in the ratification authorization. OCR in surrounding columns is poor, but this phrase is legible in the extraction and indexed original. This is a Spanish administrative writing witness, not a Moroccan vernacular sample.

sources.title: Javier Alvarado Planas and Juan Carlos Domínguez Nafría, editors: La administración del Protectorado español en Marruecos (2014)
sources.note: Official BOE volume downloaded and extracted locally (390 pages). Juan Francisco Baltar Rodríguez education chapter, printed pp. 263 to 265; María Soledad Campos Díez health chapter, printed p. 247. All chapters conservatively counted as one source. Distinguish recommendations from implemented services.

sources.title: María Dolores Jiménez Valiente: El Protectorado español en Marruecos: Educación y origen de las enseñanzas artísticas en Tetuán (2017)
sources.note: Full ten-page scholarly article directly read at University of Córdoba repository. Printed pp. 54 to 56 give school foundation, Antonio Got’s 26 December 1919 plan, entry age, materials, religious timetable and workshops. Plan remains explicitly proposed in public copy. The article’s erroneous early dynastic reversal and compressed war chronology are not adopted.

sources.title: Moroccan Ministry of Youth, Culture and Communication: Tetouan National School of Arts and Crafts
sources.note: Direct official description read. Present-day training and museum functions used as later continuity. Page compresses founding personalities and building chronology, which differ from archival scholarship; those disputed details are not used.

sources.title: Daniel Castrillejo Pérez: Los consultorios de Nador y Zoco El Had en 1912 to 1913, Sanidad Militar 65(2), 132 to 143 (2009)
sources.note: Official Ministry of Defence issue indexed original checked for vaccination, with author-uploaded full indexed text at ResearchGate publication 274079128 checked for surgery. Printed pp. 137 to 139 reproduce and analyze Valdés Lambea and Lazo García’s 1913 reports. Their racist generalizations are rejected; only particular recorded clinical activities used. Reported vaccinations are not unique people or proven universal coverage.

sources.title: Francisco Javier Martínez-Antonio: Resilient modernisation: Morocco’s agency in Red Cross projects from Hassan I to the Rif Republic, 1886 to 1926 (2014)
sources.note: Indexed full original scholarly HTML read, direct fetch fails. Rif humanitarian initiatives and blocked international mission; article sections on Rif Republic and concluding appeals. Alternate PDF is same work, not extra budget.

sources.title: Spanish Diplomatic School: Cuadernos de la Escuela Diplomática 69 (2024)
sources.note: Indexed official study read, chapter Los caladeros del Sahara Occidental y los acuerdos de pesca entre la Unión Europea y el Reino de Marruecos, historical section before footnotes 9 to 16. Supports Annual 1921, Alhucemas 1925, war to 1927, northern-zone transfer 1956 and separate Cabo Juby 1958. No current territorial claim inferred.

sources.title: Joint Hispano-Moroccan Declaration, 7 April 1956, published in BOE 4 March 1957
sources.note: Direct official PDF read, printed pp. 1386 to 1387, human PDF pp. 10 to 11. Declaration clauses 1 to 2 and additional protocol clauses 2 to 5. Signing date differs from publication date.

batchIdentityNotes.note: Independent card, no aliases. Index interval 1878 to 1914 is erroneous after May 1885. All three decoded geometries share [41.953,8.658,49.758,11.456], extending across northern Somali territories far beyond Harar city. Public overview flags both chronology and effective-control limits. Historical phases use 1875 to 1885 occupation with explicit subsequent regimes. Later house/craft survey dates retained.

One northern Moroccan feature, 1914 to 1920, bbox [-6.471,34.218,-2.327,35.862]. Historical northern protectorate 1912 to 1956. No aliases added for Tangier, Ceuta, Melilla, Spanish Sahara or southern Cabo Juby. Formal boundaries are not effective military control. Later Rif War and 1956 ending explicitly extend beyond imported interval. Spanish writing represents colonial administration, not a claim that all inhabitants spoke Spanish.
